name: Timer
purpose: A Timer raises its Tick event at a regular interval, so your code can run repeatedly without a loop that blocks the window.
whenToUse: Update a clock or countdown every second.
Refresh data or poll a status periodically.
Run a delayed action once by stopping the timer in the Tick handler.
realWorldExamples: A digital clock in a status bar.
An auto-save that runs every five minutes.
A slideshow that changes the picture every few seconds.
defaultAppearance: Timer is a non-visual component that appears in the component tray in the designer. It has no appearance at run time. It is disabled by default (Enabled = false) and has a 100 ms Interval.

commonMistakes.fix: Set Enabled = true or call Start(); a new Timer does not tick by default.

commonMistakes.mistake: Doing slow work inside Tick, which freezes the UI because Tick runs on the UI thread.
commonMistakes.fix: Keep Tick short, or start background work from it.
The Windows Forms Timer is not precise; for accuracy use a Stopwatch or another timer type.

relatedNotes.name: BackgroundWorker
relatedNotes.difference: Runs one long task on another thread; a Timer repeats a short task on the UI thread.

relatedNotes.name: ProgressBar
relatedNotes.difference: Often updated from a Timer's Tick to show elapsed time.

name: BackgroundWorker
purpose: A BackgroundWorker runs a long operation on a separate thread and reports progress and completion back on the UI thread, keeping the window responsive.
whenToUse: Run work such as file processing or a slow calculation without freezing the form.
Let the user cancel a running task.
realWorldExamples: Importing a large CSV file while a progress bar fills.
Resizing many images in the background.
Running a long report and showing 'Done' at the end.
defaultAppearance: BackgroundWorker is a non-visual component that appears in the component tray in the designer. It has no appearance at run time; its effect is seen in the controls you update from its events.

commonMistakes.mistake: Touching controls from DoWork, which throws a cross-thread exception.
commonMistakes.fix: Only update the UI in ProgressChanged and RunWorkerCompleted, which run on the UI thread.
Set WorkerReportsProgress = true (and WorkerSupportsCancellation = true for cancellation).
Check e.Error and e.Cancelled in RunWorkerCompleted before using e.Result.

relatedNotes.name: Timer
relatedNotes.difference: Repeats on the UI thread; BackgroundWorker moves work off it.

relatedNotes.name: ProgressBar
relatedNotes.difference: The usual way to display BackgroundWorker progress.

name: NotifyIcon
purpose: A NotifyIcon places an icon in the Windows notification area (system tray) so the application can run in the background, show balloon notifications and offer a quick menu.
whenToUse: Keep an application running in the tray after the window is closed or minimized.
Show a notification balloon when something happens.
Offer a right-click menu with commands like Open and Exit.
realWorldExamples: A chat app that stays in the tray with a new-message notification.
A download manager that minimizes to the tray.
A background sync tool with a status icon.
defaultAppearance: NotifyIcon is a component shown in the designer's component tray. At run time it appears as a small icon in the Windows tray; it is not visible unless you set Icon and Visible = true.

commonMistakes.mistake: Not setting an Icon, so the tray icon never appears.
commonMistakes.fix: Assign an Icon and set Visible = true.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaving a ghost icon in the tray after the app closes.
commonMistakes.fix: Set Visible = false (or Dispose) in FormClosing before exiting.

commonMistakes.mistake: Hiding the form with Hide() and not allowing the user to restore it.
commonMistakes.fix: Handle DoubleClick or a ContextMenuStrip item to Show the form and bring it to the front.

relatedNotes.name: ContextMenuStrip
relatedNotes.difference: Assign it to NotifyIcon.ContextMenuStrip for the right-click menu.

relatedNotes.name: ToolTip
relatedNotes.difference: Shows hints for controls on a form; NotifyIcon has its own Text and balloon tips.

relatedNotes.name: Timer
relatedNotes.difference: Can be used to update the icon or text at intervals.
